albums.blurb: Return to Forever was keyboardist Chick Corea's fusion vehicle, and this album captures its most celebrated lineup: Corea with Stanley Clarke on bass, Al Di Meola on guitar, and Lenny White on drums. Recorded at Caribou Ranch in Colorado in February 1976, it was the band's first record for Columbia and the last by that electric quartet, six entirely instrumental pieces built around a medieval-fantasy theme.
albums.reception: It became Return to Forever's most popular album and was certified Gold by the RIAA.

albums.blurb: Before the five-octave voice behind "Lovin' You" went solo, Riperton fronted the Chicago psychedelic-soul group Rotary Connection. Come to My Garden is her debut album, produced, arranged, and orchestrated by Charles Stepney and recorded in Chicago in late 1969 with players from Ramsey Lewis's rhythm section; it opens with "Les Fleurs," which grew into her signature song.
albums.reception: A commercial failure on release, the album has since been reappraised, with critics now regarding it as a masterpiece of orchestral soul.

albums.blurb: Mk.gee is New Jersey-raised guitarist and producer Michael Gordon, previously best known as Dijon's co-writer and co-producer. Two Star & The Dream Police, released in February 2024 on his own R&R imprint after years of self-released mixtapes and EPs, warps '80s pop, rock, and R&B through murky, heavily processed guitar into a 33-minute debut statement.
albums.reception: Pitchfork ranked it #18 on its list of the 50 Best Albums of 2024.
